text:
Marta Lopez: Heads up 1 team: Sofia is transferring from US -> JP on 2026-08-01. Question: what happens to her accrued PTO and two carryover days? Do we transfer balances, encash, or reset? Any tax/compliance notes?

Hiro Tanaka: From a manager perspective in APAC: we prefer to pro-rate and port a portion of balance when local law allows. Japan has different holiday accrual and encashment rules; usually cannot simply give cash without payroll/legal review.

Sofia Martins: I'd like to keep as much as possible as PTO since I have planned family leave in Oct. If transfer can't carry all days, can I request encashment for the remainder?

Ravi Kumar: Payroll note: encashment triggers payroll taxation and may require separate tax forms depending on country. Default flow: attempt balance transfer where permitted, otherwise offer encashment. We need employee consent for encashment and a signed form. Also need to compute accrual cutoff: last_accrual_date = 2026-07-31.

people-ops-bot: Auto-check: source country US carryover policy -> carryover cap 5 days, transfer rules -> allowed by company policy but subject to destination country law. Destination country JP has no statutory carryover recognition for incoming balances. Suggested next steps: open people-ops transfer ticket, notify payroll + legal, ask employee to choose between `transfer_partial`, `encash_partial`, or `forfeit` for any days we cannot port.

Marta Lopez: TL;DR policy we'll follow: 1) Port accruals up to local legal allowance. 2) If remainder cannot be ported, offer encashment (subject to tax/legal) or preserve as company credit valid for 6 months post-transfer (if legal allows). 3) Carryover caps are applied after porting and pro-rating. Need employee consent recorded.

legal-bot: Legal check: Japan inbound transfers require payroll review for tax withholding if encashment occurs within 12 months of transfer. Also employment contract change may affect accrued entitlement. Recommend one-off legal signoff for each inbound transfer.

Hiro Tanaka: Operational ask: if we do encashment for taxable remainder, can payroll split payments across two months to avoid pushing employee into a higher bracket? Ravi?

Ravi Kumar: We can split encashment across pay periods, but need employee approval for delayed payout. Also must emit payroll payload with `encashment_plan` and `tax_withholding` fields. Example payload we'll need:

```
employee: sofia.martins
transfer_date: 2026-08-01
accrued_hours_us: 40
carryover_days: 2
portable_hours: 24
encashable_hours: 18
encashment_option: pending_employee_choice
payroll_notes: "split_payout_allowed"
```

Marta Lopez: Good. Also policy question: is there any blackout during performance calibration / year-end where transfers or encashments are blocked? We had some confusion last year when mid-cycle transfers affected bonus/leave windows.

people-ops-bot: Policy lookup: performance calibration blackout window = 2026-07-20..2026-08-05. During blackout, non-emergency PTO approvals are discouraged and encashment payout requests are queued for post-calibration processing. Manager approval still required; payroll actions delayed until blackout end unless flagged `urgent_transfer`.

Sofia Martins: Oh — my transfer date falls inside that blackout. I do need the PTO for Oct though. Any way to mark as urgent?

Marta Lopez: If employee needs the days preserved for short-term planned leave, mark `urgent_transfer=true` and provide a brief justification. We'll route to payroll + legal with priority. Urgent flags require manager + people-ops lead signoff.

Hiro Tanaka: I'm fine to sign off if Marta ok. I'll add a manager note.

Marta Lopez: OK Sofia please reply with `@people-ops-bot transfer-pto --to=JP --date=2026-08-01 --prefer_port=true --urgent_transfer=true --justification="planned family leave Oct"` and attach consent for encashment fallback. We'll produce the official transfer ticket and legal checklist.

Sofia Martins: @people-ops-bot transfer-pto --to=JP --date=2026-08-01 --prefer_port=true --urgent_transfer=true --justification="planned family leave Oct"

people-ops-bot: Received. Created ticket POPS-8123. Notified payroll (Ravi Kumar) and legal. Required docs: signed consent form for encashment fallback. Manager approval present: Hiro Tanaka. Action items: payroll to draft encashment split plan if porting not fully allowed; legal to confirm JP compliance.

Ravi Kumar: I'll draft the payroll plan and run tax estimator. Will post back with options by EOD.

legal-bot: I'll queue the checklist for review and flag any contract clauses that block porting. Expect ping within 48 hours.

Marta Lopez: Thanks all. I'll update the international PTO transfer guidance doc with this example and add the blackout note. We'll close once payroll+legal confirm. :white_check_mark:
